gloss: to neglect; to be negligent; to fail to do

definitions.explanation: To fail to do something that should be done, often due to laziness or carelessness.

definitions.gloss: to be lazy about; to slack off on
definitions.explanation: To not put sufficient effort into a duty or task.

examples.japanese: {勉強|べんきょう}を{怠|おこた}ると、{成績|せいせき}が{下|さ}がる。
examples.english: If you neglect your studies, your grades will drop.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}{確認|かくにん}を{怠|おこた}ってはいけない。
examples.english: You must not neglect safety checks.
examples.notes: [Note: {怠|おこた}っては + いけない = must not neglect]

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}を{怠|おこた}らなければ、{必|かなら}ず{成功|せいこう}する。
examples.english: If you don't slack off on your efforts, you will surely succeed.

examples.japanese: {練習|れんしゅう}を{怠|おこた}っていたので、{試合|しあい}で{負|ま}けた。
examples.english: I had been slacking off on practice, so I lost the game.

examples.japanese: {掃除|そうじ}を{怠|おこた}っていたら、{部屋|へや}が{汚|きたな}くなった。
examples.english: I was lazy about cleaning, and the room got dirty.

examples.japanese: {日頃|ひごろ}の{運動|うんどう}を{怠|おこた}ると、{体力|たいりょく}が{落|お}ちる。
examples.english: If you slack off on daily exercise, your stamina declines.

notes:
{怠|おこた}る is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}). It takes を to mark what is being neglected.

ASPECT ({ている}):
The ている form indicates an ongoing state of neglect ({義務|ぎむ}を{怠|おこた}っている = 'is neglecting one's duty').

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [duty/task]を{怠|おこた}る (neglect ~)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {義務|ぎむ}を{怠|おこた}る (neglect a duty)
- {努力|どりょく}を{怠|おこた}る (slack off on effort)
- {注意|ちゅうい}を{怠|おこた}る (be negligent in attention)
- {健康|けんこう}{管理|かんり}を{怠|おこた}る (neglect health management)

This verb has a somewhat formal tone and is often used in written contexts. The related noun is {怠慢|たいまん} (negligence).

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {怠|おこた}っていませんでした
